Why go: a comfortable full day with fees taken care of

Wally is a twin-engine speedboat with covered seating, a captain, a deckhand and a guide. That is a step up in comfort and range from single-engine boats, and it can take up to 15 guests. Unusually for a private charter, the park and island entrance fees are included, so the only cash you need on the day is for lunch.

The four routes cover the main islands. Koh Phangan is the closest, for quiet bays and snorkelling. The southern islands day links Koh Tan's reef, Pig Island's beach and Koh Rap's long, quiet sand. Ang Thong (from 16 December) brings the Emerald Lake on Koh Mae Ko, sea caves and kayaking. Koh Tao has the clearest water, with time to snorkel the bays.

Who it suits, and who should choose something else

  • Good for: couples and families staying on the north coast, and groups who want a full day with shade and a guide.
  • Choose something else if: you're only two and want the lowest price. The Little Voyager is cheaper. Groups of 6–8 should also price the Siriwan, which includes 8 guests in the base price.
  • Staying in Lamai or the south: ask us about transfer first. It isn't automatically included.

Good to know

  • Lunch: island beach restaurants mostly take cash only. Bring enough for the group.
  • Season: February to September is the most reliable. Koh Tao crossings are often rough from October to December.
  • Viewpoints: the Ang Thong climbs are steep. Bring grippy shoes, not flip-flops.
  • Snorkelling: gear comes in adult and child sizes, but bring your own mask if you have one that fits well. A good seal makes a big difference.
